thesis: The narrator proposes testable local mechanisms and enters the selection committee, ending with an ordinary welcome whose protective or exploitative continuation remains open.

ideas.statement: Specify behavior, power, time and hidden costs; evidence must distinguish hypotheses and possible disconfirmation, not convert local findings into species destiny.
Committee choice separates commitment from unlimited availability; Mara deserves evidence-based assessment, while narrator enjoys influence and pliability.
Boundaries need not mean cruelty or universal exemption; repairing the institution cannot be assigned only to the burdened helper.
Mara asks whether analysis changes next weeks allocation; admiration differs from protection, and refusal to decide is not innocent by definition.
A sincere candidate seeks contribution beyond power games; narrator can protect or exploit this hope, closing ambiguously: I tell him we need people like him.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Fictional episodes are not population evidence; hypotheses and limited studies do not establish universal motives or inevitable outcomes.
